title: Siders Vinton County child-abuse case violent-offenders normalization pass

data.research_question: Does the June 2026 Vinton County child-abuse case involving the Siders family support inclusion in the violent-offenders dataset, and what is the current verified procedural posture?
data.method: Use the Ohio Attorney General release as the primary authority for the rescue, named adult defendants, and initial charges; use Associated Press reporting for independent corroboration and context; use the August 18 U.S. Sun report only for the newer release-motion and potential-additional-charge claim; distinguish allegations and pending charges from convictions; omit child identities and the exact home address.
classification_rules: Include named adult defendants in violent-offenders when an alleged violent or abusive offense is supported by official criminal charges and primary-source reporting.
Treat all current criminal counts as pending adjudication unless a conviction or plea is verified.
Do not convert reported potential grand-jury charges into filed charges without an official docket or charging instrument.
Do not create victim person records for minor children in this packet.
Do not publish the exact residential address where minor victims lived; retain city, county, and state only.

findings.finding: Ohio authorities located and removed 16 children during a June 30 search in Hamden and arrested four adult family members.
On July 1, Ohio authorities said each of the four adults faced 16 second-degree felony counts of endangering children.
Investigators described the matter as prolonged and extreme interfamilial neglect and abuse; AP reporting corroborated severe confinement and medical/developmental harm allegations.

An August 18 report says prosecutors told the court that additional serious felony charges against Elizabeth Siders were being considered by a grand jury; this pass did not independently verify a filed indictment containing those additional charges.
